company_verdict: Worth exactly two things and not much more: the Morningstar Indexes New Product Development team in Navi Mumbai, which has three live reqs at three levels (proof of funded headcount) and whose junior req is capped at "Up to 2 years of experience", and the two Chicago Morningstar Development Program reqs that close 5 October 2026 — one of which literally requires "A bachelor's degree to be completed no later than May 2027". Everything else in India is an immediate-start experienced-hire req, and Morningstar India's only designed fresher door (the Vashi Apprentice, REQ-057801) explicitly bars B.Tech holders and 2027 graduates, so there is no campus or internship channel here for him at all. The single highest-value action is not a portal application — it is one referral conversation inside Morningstar Indexes Navi Mumbai, because one contact covers four reqs (REQ-058340, REQ-057918, REQ-056382, AP-24776842) and is the only way a May-2027 graduate gets read against reqs written for immediate joiners. Note that score below = overlap with the POSTED wording, while rank = what he should actually spend effort on, so the Chicago reqs score high and still sit mid-list.
best_channel: Referral-driven experienced-hire req into Morningstar Indexes NPD, Navi Mumbai — submitted Dec 2026-Feb 2027 for a June/July 2027 start, not today. There is no Morningstar India campus placement channel, no India graduate/analyst programme, and no posted Jan-May final-semester internship; the one entry-level India pipeline (Apprentice REQ-057801) hard-bars "BE/B. Tech, Postgraduate, and Master's degree holders". The only true campus channel Morningstar runs is Chicago-based and closes 5 Oct 2026 — apply to it this week as a cheap lottery ticket, but do not plan around it.
may_2027_fit: Neutral-to-negative in India, and uniquely positive in exactly one Chicago req. (1) Every India posting is an ordinary experienced-hire req with no stated start window — a Workday application filed in Sep 2026 saying "available June 2027" will be screened out on availability, not on skills. His correct move is to build the referral now and submit in Dec 2026-Feb 2027, which these reqs support because Morningstar Indexes NPD has re-posted continuously through 2026 (REQ-057918 since 31 Jul, REQ-056382 since 25 Aug, REQ-058340 since 10 Sep). (2) Several India reqs require the degree in hand — REQ-057577 says "Graduation and above in any discipline", REQ-058340 says "Bachelor's degree in a quantitative, financial discipline, or engineering" — so those genuinely cannot be closed before May 2027. (3) REQ-058267 (MDP Equity Research, Chicago) is the only Morningstar req on the planet whose graduation window is his exact graduation month: "A bachelor's degree to be completed no later than May 2027", plus "We are accepting applicants with zero to two years of full-time work experience... we welcome all fields of study." No US work-authorisation clause appears on that req (unlike every Chicago internship req, which all carry "Must possess unrestricted right to work in the U.S."). DO-NOT-APPLY LIST, all timing/credential-gated: Apprentice REQ-057801 (2026 grads only, B.Tech explicitly barred — a rejection here sits in their ATS); Analyst, Private Credit Ratings REQ-057834 ("Master's or Postgraduate in Management (Finance) or CA or CFA Level 3"); Implementation Consultant REQ-057397 (bare "MBA (Finance)", and New Delhi); Compliance Associate AP-24869529 (2+ years compliance AND "two direct reports initially" — apply to the Analyst twin instead); Chicago internships REQ-058465/REQ-058268/REQ-058463 (all carry a US work-auth clause and/or require second/third year of study, and he is final-year). Also note he misses the Chicago Quantitative Research Intern 2027 (REQ-058465) purely on work authorisation despite it being the single closest content match in the whole company — "Familiarity with Python or R for data analysis", "Basic knowledge of SQL and statistical methods", "Between 0-2 years of professional working experience".

picks.title: Quantitative Analyst, New Product Development - Morningstar Indexes
picks.location: Mumbai (JD: "This position is based in our Navi Mumbai office" - Vashi, ~45 min from him)
picks.years_bar: "Up to 2 years of experience" - a CEILING, not a floor. This is the only India req that is structurally designed to exclude senior people rather than juniors.
picks.why_fit: Posted: "Up to 2 years of experience" -> he has ~13 months of internships, which is inside the band, and the ceiling means they do NOT want a 5-year hire. Posted: "Bachelor's degree in a quantitative, financial discipline, or engineering" -> B.Tech CSE (Data Science specialisation), DJSCE, CGPA 8.82 - engineering is named explicitly. Posted: "Technical proficiency with at least one programming language (Python, R or MATLAB) in addition to SQL is desirable" -> Python strong + SQL strong; R and MATLAB are alternatives, so he needs neither. Posted responsibility: "Develop new tools and capabilities to perform portfolio construction or analytics independently, including the use of statistical and machine learning techniques" -> CypherSOL, where he built ML models for transaction category and entity recognition replacing rule-based analytics, plus scikit-learn across LearnSphere and the ML Quest fake-job-posting classifier. Posted responsibility: "Publish white papers, factsheets, client presentations, and other collateral to support go-to-market plans" -> Infiheal, where he owned the Series A pitch deck and investor presentations end-to-end. Posted: "Excellent documentation habits, oral and written communication and presentation skills including ability to distil complex ideas into simple explanations" -> 4th of 400+ at Ace The Case (IIT Bombay), Winner of the Spotify/Datazen case study, Runner-Up at IES - three judged, written-and-presented analyses. Sister req REQ-056382 on the same team states verbatim that they want people "Excited by AI-first ways of working... exposure to AI agents, RAG, or workflow orchestration is a plus" - that is KOP AI (10 stateful LLM agents, RAG with page+timestamp citations) word for word, so he knows exactly how to pitch to this hiring manager.
picks.gaps: "Knowledge of institutional investing, modern portfolio theory, and portfolio construction processes" is stated FLAT, not as a preference - he has none of it beyond a Computational Finance course. "MBA from a premier institute is preferred" - no. "CFA charter or candidature (at least passed Level II) is preferred" - no, and CFA Level II is a multi-year path he should not start for this. "Hands on experience with creating Strategic Beta (Factor), ESG Indexes or similar rules-based quantitative investment strategies is preferred" - zero. And the degree itself is not conferred until May 2027 while this req reads as an immediate-start hire.
picks.learnable_edge: Index construction and portfolio theory, 3-5 weeks, and this is the ONE flat requirement he can actually close: read Morningstar's own published index methodology PDFs free at indexes.morningstar.com (Morningstar Global Markets, Dividend Yield Focus, Sustainability Index series), plus MSCI's public factor index methodology docs, plus free CFA Level I Portfolio Management reading summaries. Learn: market-cap vs equal vs factor weighting, rebalancing and reconstitution rules, buffer zones, capping, tracking error, backtest survivorship bias, the six classic factors (value, size, momentum, quality, low-vol, yield), and how an ESG index screens and re-weights. Then BUILD one: a small rules-based factor index on free NSE/Nifty constituent data in Python, backtested, written up as a 4-page methodology document in Morningstar's own house format. That single artefact simultaneously answers "knowledge of... portfolio construction processes", "Python... in addition to SQL", and "Publish white papers, factsheets". No Java, no C++, nothing heavy. Skip CFA registration - it is ~Rs 1.1 lakh for a line that is only "preferred".
picks.referral_leverage: high - a small specialist team running THREE live Navi Mumbai reqs at three levels (REQ-058340 up to 2 yrs, REQ-057918 no years stated, REQ-056382 4+ yrs) plus a Technical PM req in the same product org; that is funded, active headcount, and a referrer can route him to whichever req is open when he is available.
picks.timing: Do NOT cold-apply today - this req wants a joiner now and "available June 2027" gets auto-screened. Spend Oct-Dec 2026 on the referral and the index-methodology project, then submit Dec 2026-Feb 2027 stating "Graduating May 2027, available to join from 1 June 2027; open to a Jan-May 2027 part-time/final-semester engagement in Navi Mumbai." The re-post history (Jul, Aug, Sep 2026) says a fresh req will almost certainly be live then.

picks.title: Senior Quantitative Analyst - New Product Development - Morningstar Indexes
picks.location: Mumbai (JD: "This position is based in our Navi Mumbai office")
picks.years_bar: NONE STATED. The word "Senior" is in the title but there is no years-of-experience bullet anywhere in the posted requirements - the entire bar is a degree, a language, SQL and communication.
picks.why_fit: Posted: "Bachelor's degree in a quantitative/engineering/mathematics/statistics disciplines" -> B.Tech CSE with a Data Science specialisation and Statistics coursework, CGPA 8.82. Posted: "Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python or R)" -> Python is his strongest language (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, FastAPI across four shipped projects). Posted: "Understanding of basic financial ratios, modern portfolio theory, and portfolio construction processes is desirable but not necessary" -> explicitly waived, so his thin finance domain is not disqualifying HERE, which is the single biggest difference from REQ-058340. Posted: "Excellent documentation habits, oral and written communication and presentation skills including ability to distil complex ideas into simple explanations" -> 13x podium finishes in national case competitions and hackathons; the IIT Bombay Ace The Case result (4th of 400+, post-merger workforce restructuring, +22.4% output-to-cost) is exactly "complex idea, simple explanation, judged". Core work is "validation, curation and analysis of underlying data" for Equity and Fixed Income benchmark indexes -> that is literally his CypherSOL job, building automation pipelines that cleaned and consolidated multi-format bank statements into model-ready data.
picks.gaps: One genuine posted gap: "Proficiency in working with large, complex tables under Postgres, SQL Server." He has strong SQL and SQLAlchemy but no named Postgres or SQL Server work and nothing at production table sizes. The unposted gap is the title itself - "Senior" means the hiring manager has an internal seniority expectation the req text does not state, so without a referral a fresher CV gets binned regardless of the literal bullets. No fixed-income knowledge (duration, spread, credit quality bucketing) which the benchmark work assumes.
picks.learnable_edge: PostgreSQL at depth, 2-3 weeks, closes the ONLY posted line he misses. Install Postgres 16 locally (free), load a genuinely large public dataset (NYC TLC trip data, or AMFI daily NAV history for every Indian mutual fund scheme - the second doubles as fund-domain exposure for other Morningstar reqs), then drill: window functions (LAG/LEAD/RANK/SUM OVER PARTITION), CTEs and recursive CTEs, GROUP BY ROLLUP, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, B-tree vs composite indexes, and why a query goes from 40s to 400ms. Free: pgexercises.com, Mode Analytics SQL tutorial, the official Postgres docs. Then add a 2-day pass on SQL Server / T-SQL syntax differences (SQL Server Developer Edition is free) so he can say "Postgres and SQL Server" honestly. Same 2-3 weeks also strengthens REQ-058054, REQ-058334 and AP-24776842.
picks.referral_leverage: high - same team and same hiring manager as REQ-058340, so one referral conversation covers both, and a human is the only thing that will look past the word "Senior" at a May-2027 graduate.
picks.timing: Apply in the same Dec 2026-Feb 2027 window as REQ-058340, referral first. State "available from June 2027". If a referrer inside the team says apply now, do it immediately and let them carry the availability conversation - this req has been live since 31 Jul 2026, which suggests they are struggling to fill it and may flex.

picks.title: Morningstar Development Program - Equity Research (Campus)
picks.location: Chicago, USA ("All positions are based in our Chicago office")
picks.years_bar: "We are accepting applicants with zero to two years of full-time work experience" - zero is explicitly welcome.
picks.why_fit: This is the highest posted-wording match in the entire company. Posted: "A bachelor's degree to be completed no later than May 2027" -> he completes his B.Tech in May 2027. Not close to the window, exactly on it. Posted: "zero to two years of full-time work experience" -> he has zero full-time years (internships and freelance are not full-time employment), so he is dead centre of the band. Posted: "While we look for individuals who have an interest in investing, we welcome all fields of study" -> the usual CSE-is-not-finance objection is pre-emptively removed, and his interest in investing is evidenced, not asserted: Computational Finance coursework, a Product Management internship at Bigul benchmarking algo-trading platforms, and a Data Science internship at CypherSOL on bank-statement analytics. Crucially, unlike every Chicago INTERNSHIP req in the same family (REQ-058465, REQ-058268, REQ-058463), this req carries NO "Must possess unrestricted right to work in the U.S." clause - so the posted qualification bar does not exclude him.
picks.gaps: The killer is not on the posting: Chicago relocation and US work authorisation. He has no US degree, no OPT, no H-1B, and entry-level programme hires are very rarely sponsored - the absence of a work-auth clause is an omission he can exploit, not a promise of sponsorship. Beyond that: no finance major, no CFA Level I, no equity research writing sample, no valuation modelling (DCF, comps, sensitivity) anywhere on his resume, and no US market familiarity. Base is $83,000, which tells you they are hiring a US-domestic cohort.
picks.learnable_edge: None needed to be eligible - but do ONE weekend of work before submitting, because equity research pipelines screen on writing. Read Morningstar's free public research framework (Economic Moat, Moat Trend, Fair Value Estimate, Uncertainty Rating - all explained on morningstar.com at no cost), then write a 2-page initiating-coverage note on one Indian listed company in that exact house format: moat thesis, fair value estimate with the assumptions shown, key risks. Host it on his GitHub or personal site and link it in the application. That is ~10 hours and it is the difference between "CS student" and "candidate who already writes like us". Do NOT buy CFA Level I for this.
picks.referral_leverage: low - this is a US campus programme with a structured review process and a fixed 5 Oct cut-off; a referral cannot manufacture US work authorisation. The only referral worth chasing is an Indian-origin MDP alum in Chicago who can tell him in ten minutes whether they ever sponsor, which saves him building a false hope.
picks.timing: URGENT AND CHEAP: the req states "This role will be posted until October 5, 2026" - 11 days from today. Apply this week. State "Bachelor of Technology, Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering, expected May 2027; available to start July 2027; will require visa sponsorship." Say the sponsorship line honestly - being rejected for it costs nothing, being caught hiding it costs the relationship. Budget 30-45 minutes plus the weekend research note.

picks.title: Morningstar Development Program - Rotational Track (Campus)
picks.years_bar: None stated anywhere in the posted requirements.
picks.why_fit: The loosest requirement block Morningstar publishes anywhere. The requirements, in full, are: "A bachelor's degree" and "A resume is required to apply". He will hold a bachelor's degree in May 2027 and he has a resume. There is no graduation-year bullet, no years-of-experience bullet, and no US work-authorisation clause. Structure is "two-year program... two one-year rotations", base $71,667 - rotational analyst programmes are exactly the format that suits someone whose strength is breadth (founder's office, product management, data science, ML, freelance delivery) rather than one deep specialism, and his Infiheal work alone spans investor materials, international market entry across Korea/France/Brazil/Saudi, and B2B pipeline with IndiGo and HDFC Bank.
picks.gaps: Same decisive unposted gap as REQ-058267: Chicago-based, requires relocation and US work authorisation he does not have. Secondary: with no stated graduation year, the cohort may be built around 2026 grads who can start immediately, in which case a May-2027 finish is silently disqualifying. No US internship, no US references.
picks.learnable_edge: none needed - the posted bar is a degree and a resume. Spend the saved effort tailoring the resume's top third to rotation-friendly breadth (Infiheal founder's office, Bigul product management, the case-competition record) rather than to ML tooling.
picks.referral_leverage: low - same US campus machine, same work-authorisation wall. Not worth spending a referral favour on.
picks.timing: Also closes 5 October 2026. Submit in the same sitting as REQ-058267 - same resume, ~15 extra minutes. State expected graduation May 2027, available July 2027, visa sponsorship required.

picks.title: Data Scientist (AI & ML, Data Collection) - PitchBook
picks.years_bar: "2+ years of experience in applied data science, machine learning, NLP, or information extraction" - he has ~13 months of internships (CypherSOL DS, Sereno Volante ML) plus ~2 years freelance, so it is arguable but not clean.
picks.why_fit: The strongest technical-skill overlap of any India req, line for line. Posted: "Hands-on experience developing document intelligence or information-extraction solutions using techniques such as transformers, embeddings, RAG, LLMs, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, or agentic workflows" -> KOP AI is RAG over PDFs and YouTube with page-and-timestamp citations, orchestrating 10 stateful LLM agents in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor (60-90s down to 8-12s); LawzyAI is LLM query normalisation feeding TF-IDF retrieval over IPC/BNS sections. That single bullet is his two flagship projects. Posted: "Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn" -> all five, strongly. Posted: "Experience analyzing large, complex structured and unstructured datasets, including exploration, preprocessing, feature engineering, sampling, labeling, and dataset construction" -> CypherSOL, cleaning and consolidating multi-format bank statements into model-ready data, then building transaction-category and entity-recognition models to replace rule-based analytics; also the Spotify/Datazen win, which was large-scale EDA and cultural segmentation. Posted: "Strong understanding of... model evaluation, error analysis, and metrics such as precision, recall, F1" -> the ML Quest winning fake-job-posting classifier and LearnSphere's per-user SVM correcting domain bias. Posted: "experience with financial data... is a plus" -> CypherSOL is fintech, Bigul is algo-trading.
picks.gaps: Three named things he does not have. (1) "PyTorch or TensorFlow" is written as an AND inside the Python/SQL bullet - he has ONNX Runtime and scikit-learn but has never named either framework. (2) "Experience with Hugging Face, LangChain, or comparable NLP and LLM frameworks" - he uses Groq, ChromaDB and Llama 3.1 directly, so "comparable" is defensible but he cannot claim the named tools. (3) "2+ years of experience in applied data science" - 13 months of internships is short of the letter, and "Demonstrated experience taking a data science or machine learning solution from problem definition and experimentation through production launch and ongoing improvement" is thin: LawzyAI has a live site but no enterprise production ownership. Cloud ML environments, model monitoring and data orchestration are listed as "beneficial" only, so his Docker experience is enough there.
picks.learnable_edge: Two precise, posted-bullet-closing items, ~4 weeks total, no heavy language involved. (a) PyTorch basics, 3 weeks: the official 60-Minute Blitz, then port LearnSphere's emotion classifier or the ML Quest fake-job classifier from scikit-learn to a small PyTorch model, train it, export to ONNX (which he already knows) and publish the repo. That converts "PyTorch or TensorFlow" from a lie to a fact. (b) Hugging Face + LangChain, one weekend: run a transformers pipeline for token classification / NER (directly relevant, since the role is information extraction), then rebuild KOP AI's retrieval layer on LangChain so the resume can say "Hugging Face transformers, LangChain". Both are free. Optional third, 2 days: read the LayoutLM / document-AI primer so "document intelligence" is vocabulary he owns in interview.
picks.referral_leverage: high - PitchBook Mumbai is a smaller, newer org than core Morningstar, so the data science team is findable by name on LinkedIn and the 2+ years line is exactly the kind of soft bar a hiring manager waives when the portfolio is this on-point. Without a referral the ATS reads "13 months" and stops.
picks.timing: Immediate-start experienced-hire req, live since 17 Aug 2026 - do not cold-apply for a June 2027 start. Get the referral, and if the referrer will carry it, apply now with "available June 2027, open to a Jan-May 2027 part-time engagement". Otherwise wait for a re-post in Q1 2027. If ONE thing on this list gets a warm intro, make it this one - the technical fit is the best in the company.

picks.title: Operations Associate - International Wealth Platform
picks.location: Mumbai (JD: "Job Location: Vashi, Navi Mumbai"; "Shift Timings: 12pm to 9pm")
picks.years_bar: "Candidates with up to 2 years of experience can apply" in a dedicated Eligibility block - i.e. zero experience is explicitly acceptable. This is the most openly fresher-friendly experienced-hire req in the India set.
picks.why_fit: Posted Eligibility: "Graduation and above in any discipline" -> B.Tech qualifies once conferred, and "any discipline" removes the finance-degree objection that blocks REQ-057638 and REQ-049089. Posted Eligibility: "Candidates with up to 2 years of experience can apply" -> his ~13 months sits inside the band with room. Posted: "Robust analytical and problem-solving skills with detail orientation and accuracy" -> Winner, Analytrix'26 Datathon; Winner, Spotify Case Study at Datazen. The work is ticket-queue ownership, prioritising by severity and impact, root-cause analysis of repetitive problems and process streamlining -> that is his Bigul Product Management internship (UX friction reduction on algo workflows, feature-gap analysis, competitor benchmarking) plus the freelance registration platform where he instrumented funnel drop-off tracking and built automated WhatsApp/SMS re-engagement, which is precisely "root-cause analysis of repetitive problems" turned into a fix. Posted: "Proactive with a strong initiative... ability to manage multiple priorities" -> 10+ commercial freelance projects and Rs 6L+ client revenue while studying, plus Vice Chairperson of Trinity and Head of Marketing at DJS S4DS.
picks.gaps: "An understanding of the Financial Services marketplace that applies to Wealth Managers" - he has fintech exposure (CypherSOL, Bigul) but no wealth-management platform knowledge. "Knowledge of investment instruments across all asset classes would be advantageous" - advantageous, not required, but he has none. Salesforce and Jira appear in the role and he has neither. "Excellent computer & Excel skills" - his Excel is adequate, not advanced. "Graduation and above" means the degree must be in hand, so this genuinely cannot be applied to before May 2027. And the 12pm-9pm shift is a real lifestyle condition, not a footnote.
picks.learnable_edge: Three cheap unlocks, ~4 weeks total. (1) Salesforce Trailhead "Admin Beginner" trail - free, official, ~1 week, gives him a shareable Trailhead badge profile so "Salesforce" stops being a blank. (2) Jira - Atlassian's free Jira Work Management tier, 2-3 days; build a real ticket workflow with severity/priority schemes and SLA-style queues, which also proves the "prioritise by severity and impact" bullet. (3) Advanced Excel, 3 weeks and by far the highest-reuse item - Power Query (import, merge, unpivot, refresh), Power Pivot and the data model, XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, dynamic arrays, pivot models over a 200k-row dataset. Free via Microsoft Learn plus ExcelIsFun/Leila Gharani on YouTube. That one skill is named in six different Morningstar India reqs.
picks.referral_leverage: medium - this is a volume-hire operations team, so the portal does actually read applications and the eligibility bar is genuinely low; a referral shortens the queue and helps with the degree-timing conversation but is not the make-or-break it is for the quant and BA reqs.
picks.timing: Needs the degree conferred, so apply March-April 2027 for a June 2027 start, stating "B.Tech conferred May 2027, available to join 1 June 2027". Ops reqs at Vashi re-post constantly, so a March 2027 version of this req will exist. Do not apply now.

picks.title: Compliance Analyst, Conflicts of Interest, Global Controls (twin req: AP-24869531)
picks.location: Mumbai (4 days a week in office required; posted under DBRS Ratings GmbH, Branch India)
picks.years_bar: "At least 1 years' experience in operations, roles associated with standardization or experience in an operational business environment" - the lowest experience bar of any analyst-titled role in the India set, and the wording is broad enough that internships count honestly.
picks.why_fit: Posted: "Background or experience in process automation or AI implementation is preferred" -> this is his strongest single line anywhere at Morningstar, and almost no compliance applicant can touch it. Evidence: CypherSOL, where he built automation pipelines consolidating multi-format bank statements and replaced rule-based analytics with ML; Sereno Volante, AI and automation delivered to manufacturing clients JSW Steel and Abhijeet Plastics; and the freelance registration platform with automated WhatsApp/SMS re-engagement. Posted: "At least 1 years' experience in... an operational business environment" -> ~13 months of on-site and remote internships across four companies. Posted: "Bachelor's degree is required" -> B.Tech, May 2027. Posted: "Strong communication skills (verbal and written)" and "Strong sound judgment and a mature workplace attitude" -> Infiheal, where he engaged Brazilian and Saudi government bodies and ran IndiGo and HDFC Bank from first contact to proposal, which is stakeholder judgement under real consequence. Posted: "Ability to work effectively in a team environment" -> Vice Chairperson, Trinity; Head of Marketing, DJS S4DS. Identical twin req AP-24869531 is posted under Morningstar India Private Ltd with word-for-word the same qualifications - applying to both is harmless and doubles the chance of reaching a human.
picks.gaps: "Knowledge of securities and the finance industry" - thin; one Computational Finance course and a 6-week PM internship at Bigul. "Experience with control room functions, including preclearance of employee trades and management and use of restricted lists" - zero (flagged as "an advantage" here, which is exactly why he should apply to this Analyst version and NOT to AP-24869529, the Compliance Associate, where the same line is a flat requirement and two direct reports are added). "Experience in working with corporate policies, procedures and other guidance documents" - none. Honest career caveat: this is compliance operations, not analytics, so it is a foot in the door at Morningstar rather than the BI/BA job he actually wants - take it as a bridge, not a destination.
picks.learnable_edge: Securities and conflicts vocabulary, 3-4 weeks, genuinely closes two posted lines. NISM Series-III A (Securities Intermediaries Compliance - Non-Fund) costs roughly Rs 1,500-1,800, is an online multiple-choice exam, and is a named, verifiable Indian regulatory credential that answers "Knowledge of securities and the finance industry" outright. Alongside it, 1-2 weeks of free reading on the control-room concepts: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations on trading windows and designated persons, SEC and FINRA public guidance on restricted lists, watch lists, information barriers, pre-clearance of employee trades, and gifts-and-entertainment monitoring. That converts the "would be an advantage" line from blank to conversational. No Java, no C++, nothing over a month.
picks.referral_leverage: medium-high - the bar is low enough that the portal is not hopeless, but a referral (or the twin-req trick) is what gets a CSE resume read for a compliance seat at all. Note it sits in the DBRS/Morningstar India Mumbai compliance org, a different building network from the Indexes team, so he needs a separate contact.
picks.timing: Apply Feb-April 2027 for a June 2027 start; the req is a rolling operations hire and will re-post. State "B.Tech conferred May 2027, available 1 June 2027". If he clears NISM Series-III A before applying, put it in the resume header, not the certifications footer.

picks.title: Product Consultant, Client Service (Enterprise / Institutional)
picks.years_bar: "2-3 years of relevant experience. Experience in Financial Services/Capital markets is preferred." - he is short of the floor, not just the preference.
picks.why_fit: The named Skills block is an unusually literal match for a client-service req. Posted Skills: "API Testing (via Postman), Using Inspect in web pages to identify data mappings/source, Reading JSON/XML, Splunk, FTP Delivery mechanisms, IP whitelisting" -> he built FastAPI backends for LawzyAI and KOP AI and wrote a custom HTTP/1.1 server over raw TCP sockets plus the Git packfile protocol in GitLane, so reading JSON, tracing data mappings in a browser and testing APIs are trivial for him and rare among client-service applicants. Posted "Nice to Have": "Experience with complex information systems, understanding of basic coding, reading XML/Jason and use of Postman" -> same evidence. Posted: "Understanding of networks, web service errors, and complex software systems" -> GitLane's write-ahead push queue and offline-first sync is literally network-failure engineering. Posted: "Good understanding of financial markets and investment products (especially stocks, mutual funds, commodities, currency)" -> partially: Bigul algo-trading PM internship plus Computational Finance. Posted: "A proven record of managing clients with contractual timelines and scope" -> 10+ commercial freelance projects, Rs 6L+ revenue, and a 10,000-user registration platform shipped in 8 days.
picks.gaps: "2-3 years of relevant experience" - he has ~13 months of internships and no client-service or capital-markets service desk time. The finance domain lines are a real hole: "Fund Universe - Legal Structures - Open Ended, Close Ended, ETF's, SICAV's, Life and Pension" and "Equity/Debt - Stocks, Option Chain, Duration, Risk Statistics" - he can speak to option chains from Bigul and duration from coursework, but SICAVs and Life/Pension wrappers are blank. "Excellent skills in Microsoft Excel" - adequate, not excellent. No Splunk, no CRM. And the hard condition: "Availability to work on Saturdays, Sundays & Public holidays (on a rotating basis) is a key requirement for this role as part of a global 24x7 support operation" - weigh that honestly before applying.
picks.learnable_edge: Under one week for the entire named Skills line, which is the cheapest requirement-crossing exercise at this company. Postman: the free official Postman Learning Center course plus building a public collection against a real API (use his own LawzyAI FastAPI endpoints) - 2 days. Splunk: Splunk Free tier or the free Splunk Fundamentals 1 course, learn basic SPL search, index/sourcetype, stats and timechart - 2 days. FTP/SFTP delivery and IP whitelisting: stand up an SFTP drop with a scheduled file delivery and document the whitelisting model - 1 day. Then 2 weeks on the fund-structure vocabulary using Morningstar's own free public fund pages as the study material: open vs closed-ended, ETFs, SICAVs, unit-linked Life and Pension wrappers, share classes, TER.
picks.referral_leverage: medium - the years floor is 2-3, so a human is needed, but this is a larger client-service org that hires steadily and where a demonstrable Postman/Splunk/API story genuinely stands out in the pile.
picks.timing: Not before graduation. Apply around April-June 2027 for a June/July 2027 start. Treat it as a fallback if the Indexes route does not convert, and factor in the weekend/holiday rotation before accepting.

picks.title: Specialist, Level II (Data Level II)
picks.years_bar: "A minimum of 1-3 years of experience working in similar profiles or roles aligned to manage client expectations."
picks.why_fit: Posted: "Strong analytical, problem-solving capabilities, and excellent communication written as well as verbal & reporting skills" -> Winner of the Analytrix'26 Datathon and the Spotify/Datazen case study; 13x podium finishes. Posted project scope includes "industry/market research, market expansion, process certification, new product development support" -> that is his consulting wheelhouse: the IIT Bombay Ace The Case podium (post-merger workforce restructuring, -25% cost), the IES retail analytics runner-up (SKU rationalisation), and the Infiheal international market-entry work (Korea Market Access Program, HEC Paris/Station F, Brazilian and Saudi government engagement). Posted: "Strong learning ability and equipped with self-motivation in an independent, fast-paced work environment" -> ~2 years freelance delivery alongside a full degree. Posted: "Good command in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint etc.)" -> PowerPoint is genuinely strong (he owned Series A investor decks end to end).
picks.gaps: "Bachelor's degree or above in finance/business with knowledge in fund investment data" - he is B.Tech CSE and has zero fund-investment-data knowledge; this is the weakest degree-fit line of any role on this list. "A minimum of 1-3 years" - short. "advanced users preferred" on Excel - he is not an advanced Excel user today. "Continuously improve data collection and quality assurance process using LSS tools" - no Lean Six Sigma exposure. "Flexibility to work in shifts" plus a US shift.
picks.learnable_edge: Two items, both explicitly named in the posting. (1) Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt or a Green Belt primer, 2-4 weeks and low cost (free ASQ/Six Sigma Council body-of-knowledge PDFs, or a cheap Udemy/Coursera course with a certificate) - it directly answers the verbatim "using LSS tools" line, teaches DMAIC, SIPOC, control charts and root-cause tools, and it transfers to operations-analyst reqs at every other company on his list. That is exactly the kind of small edge-giving credential he asked for. (2) Fund investment data vocabulary, 2 weeks, free: NAV computation, TER and expense ratios, AUM, share classes, benchmark mapping, open vs closed-ended vs ETF structures, corporate actions - study it on Morningstar's own free public fund pages so the interview language is theirs. Add Advanced Excel (Power Query, Power Pivot) from the shared list to satisfy "advanced users preferred".
picks.referral_leverage: medium - a volume data-operations team at Vashi that hires continuously, so the portal is not a black hole, but the finance/business degree line means a referrer's note is what stops an auto-filter on "B.Tech CSE".
picks.timing: Apply March-May 2027 for a June 2027 start. Lower priority than picks 1-7 - take it only if the Indexes and PitchBook routes stall, because the work is data operations rather than analysis and the shift is US hours.

picks.title: Associate Content Researcher (Managed Investment Data)
picks.years_bar: "3-6 years in business/data analysis, preferably within capital markets, wealth management, or asset management domains." Per the arithmetic that matters: 13 months of internships plus part-time freelance is not 3 years. This is a NO on the posted text, not a stretch.
picks.why_fit: Listed because it is the best-shaped role in the company for what he actually wants, so he should know it exists and chase it through a human rather than the portal. Posted responsibilities: "Review and interpret business requirements to propose actionable data and process solutions", "Conduct feasibility analysis and impact analysis", "Communicate with stakeholders on the potential impacts or risks of the proposal, and make the risk mitigation plan" -> that is business analysis / consulting, matching the IIT Bombay Ace The Case work (quantified restructuring recommendation, +22.4% output-to-cost) and the Bigul feature-gap and UX-friction analysis. Posted: "A bachelor's degree in engineering, finance, economics, or business with an exceptional academic record" -> engineering is named FIRST and his CGPA is 8.82. Posted: "Experience with SQL. Basic programming, Python and database skills is preferred" -> both strong. Posted: "Experience with AI tools is a plus" -> genuinely differentiated: KOP AI's 10-agent orchestration with RAG, LawzyAI's LLM query normalisation, Google Cloud GenAI Skills Boost. Posted: "Strong quantitative and business analysis skills" and "Excellent English verbal/presentation/written communication skills" -> the entire case-competition record.
picks.gaps: "3-6 years in business/data analysis" - the single disqualifying number, and it is a range floor, so the ATS will filter him before a human sees the rest. "Profound understanding of Fund data" - none. "Understanding of Database Structure and Design" - he has SQLAlchemy and Firebase but no formal schema-design or normalisation work. "CFA/NISM/FRM/NCFM certifications or progress towards those preferred" - none held. UK shift.
picks.learnable_edge: NISM Series-V A (Mutual Fund Distributors), roughly Rs 1,500-1,800 and 3-5 weeks of part-time study for an online exam - it is the cheapest named credential at Morningstar and it closes TWO posted lines at once: "CFA/NISM/FRM/NCFM certifications or progress towards those preferred" and "Profound understanding of Fund data", because the syllabus IS fund structures, NAV, TER, share classes and scheme categorisation. Pair it with 1 week on database design fundamentals (normal forms, star vs snowflake schema, primary/foreign keys, slowly changing dimensions) using any free course, which answers "Understanding of Database Structure and Design". Neither closes the years gap - only a referral does.
picks.referral_leverage: high, and it is the ONLY route. Everything except the years number matches, and only a human can look past a years number. If he gets exactly one referral at Morningstar India outside the Indexes team, spend it here.
picks.timing: Do not cold-apply - a portal rejection on years is worse than silence. Correct play: find the Managed Investment Data team lead in Vashi on LinkedIn, send the fit case in three lines, and ask whether they would consider a strong May-2027 graduate against a junior version of this req. Realistic target window mid-to-late 2027 after 6-12 months elsewhere, or now if a referrer bites.

picks.title: Analyst, Morningstar Credit Analytics (CMBS)
picks.years_bar: "1-3 years' relevant experience in the credit research domain, with working knowledge of CMBS transactions. Credit ratings experience preferred." The domain is ANDed to the years, so both must be true.
picks.why_fit: Included for completeness because it has the lowest TOOLING bar of any research-analyst role at Morningstar and he keeps being told research analyst is a target. Posted: "Intermediate-level Excel skills" - the only tool named in the entire requirement block; no SQL, no Python, no BI tool, so nothing technical stands in his way. Posted: "Strong English-language skills, particularly writing" -> the work is monthly research reports and transaction snapshots with commentary and opinion, and his record is judged written analysis: 4th of 400+ at Ace The Case (IIT Bombay), Winner of the Spotify Case Study at Datazen, Runner-Up at IES Business School, plus the IIM Ahmedabad Innovability case with a Rs 75L Universal Design plan.
picks.gaps: He has zero credit research experience and zero CMBS exposure, and "working knowledge of CMBS transactions" is a specialist domain that cannot be faked in an interview with a ratings analyst. "Master's degree, CFA, or FRM preferred" - none, though preferred not required. No commercial real estate, no structured finance, no exposure to servicer data or rating methodologies. Verdict: he will not clear this in 2027 without a referrer who specifically wants to train a fresher.
picks.learnable_edge: 4-6 weeks of free, genuinely useful reading that makes him credible in conversation even if it does not manufacture the years: Morningstar DBRS publishes its own CMBS rating methodologies at dbrs.morningstar.com - learn DSCR, LTV, debt yield, net cash flow haircuts, tranching and the payment waterfall, subordination levels, servicer transfer and special servicing, and what a watchlist loan looks like. His Computational Finance coursework plus this reading is a credible story for a junior seat. Do NOT start CFA or FRM for this role.
picks.referral_leverage: high - this is a Mumbai offshore-analytics team that hires in volume, so a referral is the only thing that gets him past the "no credit experience" auto-filter; without one the application is wasted. Separately, note that REQ-057834 (Analyst, Private Credit Ratings) is the same Navi Mumbai building but gates on "Master's or Postgraduate in Management (Finance) or CA or CFA Level 3" - that one he should never apply to.
picks.timing: Only if a referrer inside Morningstar Credit Analytics explicitly invites him, and then for a June 2027 start. Otherwise skip entirely and put the hours into picks 1, 2 and 5.

skills_to_learn.skill: Advanced Excel - Power Query, Power Pivot / data model, XLOOKUP and INDEX-MATCH, dynamic arrays, scenario and pivot modelling
skills_to_learn.why: The single most repeated requirement across the entire Morningstar India set, named in at least six postings: REQ-057577 ("Excellent computer & Excel skills"), REQ-057638 ("Good command in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint etc.); advanced users preferred"), REQ-058210 ("Intermediate-level Excel skills" - the ONLY tool that req names), REQ-058048 ("Excellent skills in Microsoft Excel"), REQ-049089 ("Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint") and the FP&A req AP-24305912 ("Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel is essential"). Also note the flip side: do NOT learn Tableau for Morningstar - the Apprentice req says the house stack is "Excel, SQL, and Power BI" and the FP&A req lists "Tableau, or PowerBI" as alternatives, so his existing PowerBI already satisfies every BI line here. Push PowerBI high on the CV for every Morningstar application.
skills_to_learn.effort: 3 weeks, ~1 hour a day, ending with one real artefact
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Microsoft Learn Excel modules (official), plus ExcelIsFun and Leila Gharani on YouTube for Power Query and Power Pivot. Deliverable: take a 200k+ row public dataset (AMFI daily mutual fund NAV history is ideal because it doubles as fund-domain study), build a refreshable Power Query pipeline, a Power Pivot data model with DAX measures, and a one-page dashboard. That artefact is the evidence, not the claim.

skills_to_learn.skill: PostgreSQL / SQL Server at depth - window functions, CTEs, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, indexing, large-table work
skills_to_learn.why: Closes the ONLY posted line he misses on REQ-057918 ("Proficiency in working with large, complex tables under Postgres, SQL Server"), and reinforces REQ-058340 ("...in addition to SQL is desirable"), REQ-058054 ("Proficiency in Python and SQL"), REQ-058334 ("Experience with SQL" and "Understanding of Database Structure and Design") and the Technical PM req AP-24776842 ("Hands-on experience with SQL and/or data analysis tools"). Five postings from one three-week block of work.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: install PostgreSQL 16 locally and SQL Server Developer Edition (also free) for two days of T-SQL syntax differences. Drill on pgexercises.com and the Mode Analytics SQL tutorial. Load NYC TLC trip data or AMFI NAV history, then practise LAG/LEAD/RANK/SUM OVER PARTITION, recursive CTEs, GROUP BY ROLLUP, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and composite indexes until he can show a query going from 40s to sub-second.

skills_to_learn.skill: Index construction and portfolio theory - MPT, factor / smart-beta weighting, rebalancing rules, ESG index mechanics
skills_to_learn.why: Closes the one FLAT (non-preferred) domain requirement on REQ-058340 ("Knowledge of institutional investing, modern portfolio theory, and portfolio construction processes"), covers the softened line on REQ-057918 ("desirable but not necessary"), and is the interview language for the whole Morningstar Indexes Navi Mumbai team including REQ-056382 and AP-24776842 - i.e. it unlocks his top two picks plus the team he is targeting for a referral.
skills_to_learn.effort: 3-5 weeks, ending with a written methodology document
skills_to_learn.resource: All free: Morningstar's own published index methodology PDFs at indexes.morningstar.com (Global Markets, Dividend Yield Focus, Sustainability series), MSCI's public factor index methodology docs, and free CFA Level I Portfolio Management reading summaries. Then BUILD one: a rules-based factor index on free NSE constituent data in Python, backtested, and write it up as a 4-page methodology doc in Morningstar's own format. Do not register for CFA (~Rs 1.1 lakh) for a line that is only "preferred".

skills_to_learn.skill: Fund data vocabulary + NISM Series-V A (Mutual Fund Distributors) certification
skills_to_learn.why: The cheapest named credential at this company. Directly answers REQ-058334's "CFA/NISM/FRM/NCFM certifications or progress towards those preferred" AND its "Profound understanding of Fund data", plus REQ-057638's "Bachelor's degree or above in finance/business with knowledge in fund investment data", plus REQ-057577's "Knowledge of investment instruments across all asset classes" and REQ-058048's "Fund Universe - Legal Structures - Open Ended, Close Ended, ETF's, SICAV's, Life and Pension". Four postings, and it is the fastest way for a B.Tech CSE candidate to stop reading as a non-finance applicant.
skills_to_learn.resource: NISM's own free downloadable workbook for Series-V A, exam booked online at certifications.nism.ac.in. Supplement with Morningstar's free public fund pages to learn NAV, TER, AUM, share classes, benchmark mapping and scheme categorisation in Morningstar's own terminology.

skills_to_learn.skill: PyTorch basics, plus Hugging Face transformers and LangChain
skills_to_learn.why: Closes the two named bullets he misses on REQ-058054 (PitchBook Data Scientist), the best technical fit in the company: "Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and PyTorch or TensorFlow" and "Experience with Hugging Face, LangChain, or comparable NLP and LLM frameworks". Everything else on that req he already satisfies through KOP AI, LawzyAI, LearnSphere and CypherSOL. One req, but it is the highest-ceiling req on the list.
skills_to_learn.effort: 3-4 weeks for PyTorch; one weekend for Hugging Face + LangChain
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: the official PyTorch "60-Minute Blitz" then fast.ai Part 1. Deliverable: port the LearnSphere emotion classifier or the ML Quest fake-job-posting classifier from scikit-learn to a small PyTorch model, train it, export to ONNX (which he already knows) and publish the repo. Then run a Hugging Face transformers token-classification/NER pipeline (directly on-topic for an information-extraction role) and rebuild KOP AI's retrieval layer on LangChain.

skills_to_learn.skill: Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt (or Green Belt primer) - DMAIC, SIPOC, root-cause tools, control charts
skills_to_learn.why: REQ-057638 names it verbatim: "Continuously improve data collection and quality assurance process using LSS tools." It also gives him structured vocabulary for the process-improvement language in REQ-057577 ("identify root causes of repetitive problems", process streamlining) and REQ-058381. Low cost, fast, and it transfers to operations-analyst roles at every other company on his shortlist - exactly the kind of small edge-giving certification he asked for.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free body-of-knowledge PDFs from the Council for Six Sigma Certification and ASQ's public materials; or a cheap Udemy/Coursera Yellow Belt course for a shareable certificate. Apply DMAIC to a real artefact - e.g. document the defect-reduction story from his CypherSOL bank-statement cleaning pipeline in SIPOC form.

skills_to_learn.skill: Postman, Splunk basics, SFTP delivery and IP whitelisting
skills_to_learn.why: Covers the ENTIRE named Skills line of REQ-058048 in one week: "API Testing (via Postman), Using Inspect in web pages to identify data mappings/source, Reading JSON/XML, Splunk, FTP Delivery mechanisms, IP whitelisting" - he already owns the JSON/XML and web-inspect half through FastAPI and GitLane. Highest ratio of posted-requirement-coverage to hours of any item here.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Postman Learning Center official course - build and publish a public collection against his own LawzyAI FastAPI endpoints. Splunk Free tier or Splunk Fundamentals 1 for basic SPL (search, index/sourcetype, stats, timechart). Stand up an SFTP drop with a scheduled delivery and write up the IP-whitelisting model.

skills_to_learn.skill: Jira, Confluence and Salesforce Trailhead (Admin Beginner)
skills_to_learn.why: Named across three postings: REQ-057577 (Salesforce and Jira in the role), AP-24776842 Technical Product Manager ("Experience using tools such as JIRA, Confluence, SQL editors, BI/reporting platforms"), and AP-24305912 FP&A ("experience with Oracle/Hyperion, Salesforce, Tableau, or PowerBI is preferred" - his PowerBI already covers the BI half). Cheap gap-fillers that stop three blanks on the CV.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Salesforce Trailhead "Admin Beginner" trail gives a public badge profile; Atlassian's free Jira Work Management and Confluence tiers - build a real ticket workflow with severity and priority schemes and a linked Confluence spec, which doubles as evidence for "prioritise by severity and impact".

skills_to_learn.skill: Conflicts-of-interest and control-room vocabulary + NISM Series-III A (Securities Intermediaries Compliance)
skills_to_learn.why: Closes both soft gaps on REQ-058381 and its twin AP-24869531 - "Knowledge of securities and the finance industry" (which NISM Series-III A answers as a named credential) and "Experience with control room functions, including preclearance of employee trades and management and use of restricted lists" (flagged as an advantage on the Analyst version). Two reqs for the same role means two shots at a human.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free reading: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations on trading windows and designated persons, SEC and FINRA public guidance on restricted lists, watch lists and information barriers. Paid-but-cheap: NISM Series-III A workbook (free download) and online exam.

skills_to_learn.skill: Morningstar's own equity research framework - Economic Moat, Moat Trend, Fair Value Estimate, Uncertainty Rating
skills_to_learn.why: Not a qualification bullet anywhere, but it is what decides the Chicago MDP Equity Research application (REQ-058267), which closes 5 October 2026 and is the only Morningstar req whose graduation window is literally "no later than May 2027". Equity research pipelines screen on writing samples, and he currently has none.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free on morningstar.com - read the published moat and fair-value methodology plus half a dozen real analyst notes, then write a 2-page initiating-coverage note on one Indian listed company in that exact house format (moat thesis, fair value with assumptions shown, key risks) and link it from the application.

referral_strategy: A referral is not optional at Morningstar India - it is the whole game, because every India posting is an experienced-hire req with a years floor and none of them are tagged campus, so a May-2027 graduate applying cold is filtered on availability before a human reads a line. Four concrete targets, in priority order. (1) MORNINGSTAR INDEXES, NEW PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, NAVI MUMBAI - the highest-leverage single contact at the entire company, because one referrer covers four live reqs (REQ-058340 up to 2 yrs, REQ-057918 no years stated, REQ-056382 4+ yrs, and Technical Product Manager AP-24776842). Search LinkedIn for current employees with \"Morningstar Indexes\" in the title or description located in Mumbai/Navi Mumbai, filtered to Quantitative Analyst, Senior Quantitative Analyst, Lead Quantitative Analyst, and Director/Head of Index Product. Message hook: the REQ-056382 posting itself says the team wants people \"Excited by AI-first ways of working... exposure to AI agents, RAG, or workflow orchestration is a plus\" - so his opening line is KOP AI (10 stateful LLM agents orchestrated in parallel, RAG with page-and-timestamp citations, 60-90s to 8-12s) and a link to the factor-index methodology doc he is going to build. That is a message an index quant will actually reply to. (2) DJSCE AND MUMBAI-CAMPUS ALUMNI - use the LinkedIn alumni tool on the Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering page filtered to company = Morningstar, and repeat for the neighbouring feeder colleges whose societies he already has contacts in from competitions he won: KJ Somaiya (Datazen/Spotify case), Thakur College Society for Data Science (Analytrix'26), plus VJTI, SPIT and TSEC. Vashi hires heavily off exactly these campuses even though the reqs are not tagged campus. Ask alumni two things: does Morningstar India run any Jan-May final-semester internship informally, and will the Indexes/Data teams look at a June-2027 joiner. (3) PITCHBOOK MUMBAI DATA SCIENCE - for REQ-058054, the best technical fit in the company. PitchBook Mumbai is a smaller, newer org than core Morningstar, so the DS team is individually findable; target Data Scientist, Senior Data Scientist and Manager, Data Science with \"PitchBook\" in the company field and Mumbai in location. The 2+ years bar is the only obstacle and it is precisely the kind a hiring manager waives when the portfolio matches the bullets line for line. (4) MORNINGSTAR INDIA TALENT ACQUISITION - search LinkedIn for \"Talent Acquisition\" or \"Campus Recruiter\" at Morningstar, Mumbai. Send ONE question, not a resume dump: \"Does Morningstar India take final-semester interns between January and May 2027, and do the Navi Mumbai Indexes NPD reqs consider candidates joining in June 2027?\" That single answer is worth more than ten portal applications, because if the answer is no, he stops spending time on India Morningstar entirely and redirects to companies that do run 2027 graduate programmes. PARALLEL, NON-LINKEDIN ACTION: tell the DJSCE placement cell (TPO) to approach Morningstar India for the 2027 batch NOW - Morningstar runs a serious campus machine in Chicago and an apprenticeship pipeline in Vashi, so the appetite for entry-level hiring exists in India even though the reqs are not posted as campus roles; an institutional ask from a target college is a different lever than an individual application. WHERE A REFERRAL WILL NOT HELP: the two Chicago MDP reqs (REQ-058267, REQ-058222) - no referrer can create US work authorisation, so do not spend a favour there; and the Apprentice req REQ-057801, where the B.Tech exclusion is absolute regardless of who refers him.
